source: WHO Weekly Epidemiological Record No. 43, 26 October 1973 - Table 1, Cholera Cases 1973 (Four-Weekly Periods) (WER 48:414)
processing_notes: Source states: 'Table 1. Cholera Cases, 1973 (Four-Weekly Periods) -- Africa - Afrique ... Malawi ... [period] 11 ... 22 ... Total 22' - interpreted as 22 sCh cases. THE FIRST CHOLERA CASES EVER RECORDED IN MALAWI. In WER's within-year table for 1973 Malawi is absent from four-weekly periods 1-10 and appears only in period 11 with 22 cases and a running total of 22, consistent with WER 49(27)'s statement that Malawi reported cholera 'for the first time in 1973 ... in October'. TL/TR bracket four-weekly period 11 up to the issue date of 26 October 1973; the exact period boundaries are not printed. Malawi's full-year 1973 total was 371 (WER 49(27) Table 1, also in WHO GHO and the JHU baseline at ./data/MWI/cholera_data_jhu.csv Index 1228), so the remaining ~349 cases fell in November-December 1973. SUB-PERIOD of the JHU 1973 annual row - do not sum with it.

source: WHO African Region situation report: Cholera situation in Malawi, 24 April 2002 (via ReliefWeb)
processing_notes: Source states: 'The current season which started on 28 October 2001 is described as the worst that the country has ever faced with 32,968 cases reported and 980 deaths recorded as at 7 April 2002, thus resulting in an unacceptable 2.97 CFR' - interpreted as 32968 sCh cases, 980 deaths. Near-final national total of the 2001-02 epidemic, four weeks after the interim at Index 110 (22,023 / 609 to 9 March 2002) - so roughly 11,000 further cases and 371 further deaths occurred in the four weeks to 7 April 2002. Source adds 'all of the 27 districts have reported at least one case except Rumphi in North' and that 'Vibrio cholerae 01 Ogawa biotype is responsible'. Index 3 carries the same epidemic as a calendar-block 2001-2002 total of 33,546 cases and 968 deaths; the death counts differ (980 here at 7 April vs 968 for the whole season), which is a genuine inconsistency in the underlying reporting and is recorded rather than reconciled. OUTBREAK CUMULATIVE - do not sum with Index 3, Index 110 or the JHU 2001/2002 annual rows.

source: WHO African Region situation report: Cholera situation in Malawi, 24 April 2002 (via ReliefWeb)
processing_notes: Source states: 'Lilongwe district where the capital city is located leads all other districts in disease burden with 5537 cases and 160 deaths' - interpreted as 5537 sCh cases, 160 deaths. District-level burden in the 2001-02 epidemic - the only district figure available for that epidemic, and the highest-burden district. 5,537 of the national 32,968 (16.8%) as at 7 April 2002. The report adds that 'districts in the centre and south of the country are more affected ... especially those in close proximity to natural lakes where the epidemics usually start before spreading to other districts', and that all 27 districts except Rumphi had reported at least one case. District subset - do not sum with national rows.

source: IFRC Southern Africa: Cholera Appeal No. 03/2000, 10 February 2000 (via ReliefWeb)
processing_notes: Source states: 'Cholera has again broken out in the southern Africa region in 2000. Zimbabwe reported 955 cases and 51 deaths. Mozambique has recorded 591 cases and 15 deaths. In Malawi, 723 cases have been reported with 19 deaths.' - interpreted as 723 sCh cases, 19 deaths. Early-2000 interim national count, the only sub-annual figure located for the 1999-2000 season. AMBIGUITY RECORDED: the framing 'in 2000' supports a calendar-year-to-date reading, which is the TL/TR used here, but the source does not state a start date and the figure could be season-to-date from the October-November 1999 onset. WHO GHO and the JHU baseline give Malawi 2,391 cases and 56 deaths for the whole of calendar 2000, so 723/19 by 10 February is a plausible interim either way. Confidence 0.8 (Level 2 source, interpretive TL). SUB-PERIOD - do not sum with the JHU 2000 annual row. Partially supersedes the count-less 1999-2000 entry in ./data/MWI/cholera_presence_ai.csv.

processing_notes: Source states: 'Table 1 Summary of cholera cases and deaths by district [District | Number of cases | Number of deaths]: Mzimba 486/3; Ntchisi 68/2; Kasungu 90/6; Chitipa 91/3; Chikwawa 748/11; Mchinji 394/16; Phalombe 302/14; Zomba 759/28; Mwanza 120/5; Thyolo 1,520/36; Dowa 1,349/39; Mulanje 936/42; Karonga 1,403/25; Nsanje 607/21; Rumphi 932/18; Ntcheu 1,926/56; Neno 733/14; Mangochi 8,182/120; Dedza 2,124/95; Chiradzulu 1,426/41; Likoma 204/2; Machinga 2,708/104; Nkhotakota 1,461/56; Blantyre 8,975/190; Nkhata Bay 1,628/49; Balaka 4,111/81; Salima 3,591/97; Lilongwe 12,683/558' - interpreted as 12683 sCh cases, 558 deaths. Provincial subset - do not sum with national row. THE COMPLETE 28-DISTRICT TABLE for the 2022-23 epidemic, from the cleaned PHIM/Ministry of Health national cholera surveillance database (https://cholera.health.gov.mw/surveillance) as extracted by the authors on 20 May 2023; the paper's Figure 1 caption states 'Data were obtained from the Public Health Institute of Malawi (PHIM), Malawi Ministry of Health (MoH) data on May 20, 2023'. TL is set to 2022-03-03, the Ministry of Health outbreak declaration date used throughout this dataset; the paper's own figures span January 2022 to May 2023. ARITHMETIC CHECK AND ITS RESOLUTION: the 28 districts sum to 59,557 cases and 1,732 deaths. The same paper's national figures are 59,156 cases and 1,771 deaths (accessed 30 May 2024) and, for the CFR calculation, 1,759 of 58,730. processing_notes: Source states: 'Since the start of the 2025/26 Cholera season on 1 November 2025, Malawi has recorded a cumulative total of 3,013 local cholera cases, including 25 deaths (13 facility and 12 community). Of these, 319 were laboratory-confirmed cases, with 5 facility deaths, while 460 were epidemiologically linked cases. ... A total of 774 patients have recovered and were discharged. Based on the cumulative 3,013 cases and 13 facility deaths the case fatality ratio (CFR) is 0.43%.' - interpreted as 3013 sCh cases, 319 cCh confirmed cases, 25 deaths. National total - includes provinces not individually listed. Final cumulative for the 2025/26 cholera season. IMPORTANT REVISION: this bulletin restates the season death toll as 25 (13 facility + 12 community) where every earlier bulletin, including epi-week 33 published only ten days before, reported 5 deaths 'recorded between 9 January and 29 March 2026'. The 5 figure was facility deaths among laboratory-confirmed cases only; the 25 figure adds community deaths and suspected-case deaths. Rows carrying the old 5 (Index 57, 78, 93, 111 and others) are therefore not wrong, they use the narrower definition. The 0.43 percent CFR the bulletin prints is 13/3,013, i.e. facility deaths over all cases - a third definition again. deaths=25 is recorded here as the widest and latest count; CFR is computed as 25/3,013 = 0.83 percent. Cross-border cases are excluded from the 3,013, as PHIM states they are 'In addition to locally reported cases'.
